readings: Join fees to their orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`; drop fees with no matching order) and group by time in force (`orders.timespan`). For each group, take the average of `rebrate` / `feerate` (ignoring missing values) and the number of joined fee records in the group. Keep only the groups whose fee-record count is strictly above the average of that count across all groups. Return one row with three values for those kept groups: the average of their average ratios, the sum of their fee-record counts, and the average amount by which their count exceeds the cross-group average count. Don't round anything.
queries:
WITH g AS (
  SELECT o.timespan AS ts,
         AVG(f.rebrate / f.feerate) AS avg_ratio,
         COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.timespan
),
a AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM g
)
SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios,
       SUM(g.cnt) AS total_count,
       AVG(g.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess
FROM g, a
WHERE g.cnt > a.avg_cnt;
